title: Workspace gremlin also bites next_action: loops aren't workspace-pinned
summary: Finding (2026-06-10): the per-session workspace pin (mcp-core makeCall) only covers MUTATING tool calls. The loop registry stores no workspace, and next_action evaluates every loop against the daemon's GLOBAL state.workspace — when another session flipped it, our loop's heartbeat saw a 0-task graph, returned "stop: DAG drained", and demoted the loop mid-flight. Recovery: POST /workspace to re-pin, then loop_start with the same loopId to reactivate. Proper fix: store workspace on each loop at loop_start and evaluate that loop's decisions against ITS workspace graph, not the global pointer. Related: [[loop bootstrap race]] — second liveness bug in the same sweep/heartbeat area. Also note the 10-minute stale-claim sweep releases claims of long-running workers that don't refresh lastChanged; re-calling start_task with the same agent_id refreshes it.
